tagline.text: A limestone peak above Wawa Gorge and the legend of the independence cave

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Wawa, Rodriguez, Rizal, in the Pamitinan Protected Landscape

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (rocks are slippery in the rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,500 (transport, registration, a share of the guide fee and meals, per person)

children.text: Mount Pamitinan is a limestone peak about 426 meters high in Wawa Gorge, Rodriguez, about 34 kilometers from Manila. It is an easy day hike of about two hours to the summit, but the rocky sections call for gloves and a guide.

Mount Pamitinan is a mountain about 426 meters high in Barangay Wawa, Rodriguez (formerly Montalban), Rizal. It sits at the western edge of the Sierra Madre range, with its twin, Mount Binacayan at about 424 meters, facing it across the gap. The narrow gorge where the Marikina River passes between the two mountains is Wawa Gorge (also called Montalban Gorge), and the area became the Pamitinan Protected Landscape, about 609 hectares, under Proclamation No. 901 in 1996. It lies about 34 kilometers northeast of central Manila, so you can leave at dawn and return the same day.

The mountain means more to Filipinos than an ordinary hiking spot. A legend tells of the giant Bernardo Carpio trapped between the two mountains, and it is said that earthquakes are him pushing the rocks apart. It is also said that Andres Bonifacio and Katipunan members declared independence in Pamitinan Cave on April 12, 1895. It is reported that a revolution-era inscription, "Viva la Independencia," is carved in the inner chamber called Bulwagan, but accounts of this differ between sources, so listen to your local guide's explanation as well.

The route starts in Wawa village, passes through forest and an old balete (strangler fig) tree, and climbs through rock sections onto a limestone ridge. One hiking guide says the summit takes about 1.5 to 2.5 hours, rates the difficulty 3 out of 9, and gives the trail a class of 1 to 4. From the top you get a 360-degree view: Mount Hapunang Banoy to the north, distant Mount Arayat, the Sierra Madre to the east and south, and the Wawa River and Mount Binacayan to the west. Rock-climbing and bouldering routes are also available and known among climbing fans. The protected landscape was originally part of the Mariquina Reserve, set up in 1904 to protect the Marikina River watershed. The forest includes lowland dipterocarp trees such as tanguile and bagtikan, and birds such as the scale-feathered malkoha and peregrine falcon have been seen, so it is also known as a birdwatching site.

This guide is for travelers looking for a hike close to central Manila and for people who want to combine it with Wawa Dam for a day. If you are used to rocky peaks, it is not difficult, but you should know in advance about the Philippine heat, guide rules and the reservation system. Registration methods, fees and whether the area is open change from year to year, so check the latest guidance on the official DENR Pamitinan channels before you leave. In February 2021 the area reopened after pandemic closures, with online reservations, age limits and visitor caps reportedly in place. There are also reports that the registration area opened at 4 a.m. and stopped accepting people at noon, so avoid arriving late.

blocks.title: Forest path and the balete tree

children.text: The first part of the hike is a shaded forest path, passing an old balete tree and a rock-climbing area. Going through this section early in the morning, away from the midday heat, is much easier. Some poison ivy (lipa) is known to grow in the forest, so it is better to wear clothes that cover your arms and legs. Around the balete's roots there are many birds and insects, so it is a nice place to stop and listen to the forest.

A junction where you rest just before the rock sections. Beyond this point the rock begins in earnest, so drink water and check your gloves and shoes. There is no water on the mountain, so carry plenty from the start.

You climb limestone rock mixed with bamboo and thorny plants, using your hands. Many sections have no ropes, and beginners may need help. When it has rained the rock is very slippery, and there are cases of hikers turning back, so check the weather.

The protected landscape has Pamitinan Cave and Bat Cave, described as having stalactites, stalagmites and rimstone pools. Visit the caves with a guide and do not enter on your own. Bat Cave is known to be reachable only in summer, when the dam's water level is low.

Many people cool off at Wawa Dam after the hike. It is an old water-supply dam, begun in 1904 and in operation from 1909, and is now a recreation spot. It is described as having bamboo rafts and places to rest by the water, and it is covered in a separate article.

Mount Pamitinan has designated routes for rock climbing and bouldering. It is safer for people with equipment and experience to climb with a guide. Ordinary travelers will find the hiking route enough.

After registering, you walk to the trailhead. Wawa Dam is reached by a short ridge walk.
This is a rocky mountain, so climbing in the dry season is safer. In the rainy season the limestone is wet and very slippery, and streams can swell.
Midday from March to May is very hot. Start at dawn and do not linger long on the summit. Weekdays are quieter at the registration desk.

The most comfortable hours are from just before sunrise until around 11 a.m., and Wawa Gorge lit by sunlight after sunrise photographs well from the summit. On holidays and weekends the registration desk gets crowded and visitor caps may apply, so a weekday is easier.

Wawa village has few places to stay, so most people make a day trip from Manila. If you need a place to sleep, there are small lodgings in Rodriguez and Montalban, so check recent reviews on booking sites. Camping and overnight stays on the mountain are described as restricted, so check the local rules.

At the entrance to Wawa village, small eateries and shops sell packed meals, instant noodles and drinks. There is no water or food on the mountain, so prepare plenty of lunch and water in Manila or Montalban. You must carry your trash out.

After the hike you can eat at the entrance to Wawa village or in Montalban town. There are few hearty restaurants like the ones at the foot of Korean mountains, so expect simple places, and check hygiene and prices before you eat. Shops around Wawa Dam sell water, drinks and snacks.

Bring grippy hiking shoes, gloves, a hat, at least 2 liters of water, emergency food, a power bank and a light rain jacket. Trekking poles can get in the way on the rock, so fold them and put them in your bag.
Start at dawn to avoid the midday heat.
Gloves are essential for the limestone rock and thorny plants. You can also buy them at the local DENR office.
Wear grippy hiking shoes instead of sandals.
Carry at least 2 liters of water. There is no water source on the mountain.
Start at the Wawa protected-area office to confirm same-day registration, accredited guide assignment and fee items. Ask if separate barangay registration is required.
There have been periods with online reservations and visitor caps, so check the official DENR Pamitinan channels before you leave.
Phone signal is generally good, but bring a power bank.
Stay with your guide and do not leave the trail.

Reports say Pamitinan Protected Landscape reopened on September 19, 2026 after a rockfall-related closure and safety checks. At the protected-area registration office in Wawa, check which routes are open, guide assignment and current hiking and guide fees. Delay your trip after heavy rain and stay on designated trails.
The rocks are sharp, and without gloves your hands are easily hurt.
There is no water or shelter on the mountain, so guard against dehydration and heatstroke.
Beginners can be at risk on the rock sections without protection, so always go with a guide.
At times, pregnant women, children and older people have been restricted from entering, depending on the guidelines.
Fees, reservation rules and whether the area is open change often, so check the latest announcements.
There are no emergency facilities on the mountain, so tell your group your plan and expected descent time, and turn back if you feel unwell.
An old dam in the same Wawa Gorge, good for resting after the hike. It is known for bamboo rafts and swimming.
